_comment: === TEST FILE: Check hierarchy â€” B-check substitutes overdue A-check ===
Four aircraft with mixed A/B threshold states:
AC0: A_init=27001 (A overdue), B_init=42001 (B also overdue)
-> HEURISTIC (D>C>B>A priority): B-check (2880 min) scheduled, resets both counters.
-> MILP --no-check-hierarchy: B-check AND A-check required on separate days.
-> MILP with hierarchy ON: B-check alone covers A requirement (1 event, not 2).
AC1: A_init=0, B_init=42001 (only B overdue)
-> B-check regardless of hierarchy flag.
AC2: A_init=26800, B_init=0  (A triggered mid-horizon after 200 min flight)
-> 26800 + 200 = 27000 >= threshold -> A-check on arrival at C.
AC3: all zeros, starts at C â€” free aircraft for C->B outbound legs.
NOTE: --no-check-hierarchy has NO effect on the heuristic (heuristic always
uses D>C>B>A priority and natural counter resets). The flag only changes
MILP constraint c_hierarchy.
Heuristic (both flags give identical output):
py -3 heu180h.py --data inputsABCD/ABCD_check_hierarchy_test.json --no-show
MILP comparison (observe AC0 gets 1 vs 2 check events):
py -3 heu180h.py --mode milp --data inputsABCD/ABCD_check_hierarchy_test.json --solver cplex --no-show
py -3 heu180h.py --mode milp --data inputsABCD/ABCD_check_hierarchy_test.json --solver cplex --no-check-hierarchy --no-show
Horizon: ~10 days.  Station_Capacity: C=4.
